+def test_runner_stream_lifecycles():
+    shared = BytesIO()
+    wrapper = _NamedTextIOWrapper(
+        shared, encoding="utf-8", name="<first>", mode="w"
+    )
+    other_wrapper = _NamedTextIOWrapper(
+        shared, encoding="utf-8", name="<second>", mode="w"
+    )
+
+    del wrapper
+    gc.collect()
+
+    other_wrapper.write("shared")
+    other_wrapper.flush()
+    assert shared.getvalue() == b"shared"
+
+    runner = CliRunner()
+    with runner.isolation() as streams:
+        click.echo("stdout")
+        click.echo("stderr", err=True)
+
+    gc.collect()
+
+    assert streams[0].getvalue() == b"stdout\n"
+    assert streams[1].getvalue() == b"stderr\n"
+    assert streams[2].getvalue() == b"stdout\nstderr\n"
+
+    old_streams = sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr
+    logger = logging.Logger("click.stream-lifecycles", level=logging.ERROR)
+    handlers = []
+    thread_errors = []
+
+    @click.command()
+    @click.option("--fail", is_flag=True)
+    def cli(fail):
+        handler = logging.StreamHandler()
+        handlers.append(handler)
+        logger.addHandler(handler)
+        logger.error("logged")
+        click.echo("stdout")
+
+        if fail:
+            raise RuntimeError("fail")
+
+    first_result = runner.invoke(cli, ["--fail"])
+    assert first_result.exit_code == 1
+    assert first_result.output == "logged\nstdout\n"
+    assert (sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr) == old_streams
+
+    gc.collect()
+
+    def write_after_invoke():
+        try:
+            handlers[0].stream.write("thread\n")
+            handlers[0].flush()
+        except Exception as e:
+            thread_errors.append(e)
+
+    thread = threading.Thread(target=write_after_invoke)
+    thread.start()
+    thread.join()
+
+    second_result = runner.invoke(cli)
+    assert second_result.exit_code == 0
+    assert second_result.output == "logged\nstdout\n"
+    assert (sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr) == old_streams
+    assert not thread_errors
+
+    for handler in handlers:
+        logger.removeHandler(handler)
+        handler.close()
+
+
